# On-call handoff — gateway 503s

**Incident date:** 2026-03-14
**Status at handoff:** ONGOING — still failing at end of available logs
**Severity:** ~83% of API traffic failing

## Root cause

Gateway config generation 119 flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest` from `false` to `true`.

That makes the gateway open a new upstream connection for every request instead of reusing pooled ones. The pool is only 20 connections. It can't keep up.

The gateway logged the effect itself:

```
03:02:30.904Z WARN pool connection churn: 4180 opens in the last 5m, baseline is 40
```

100x the normal connection rate. The pool saturates, requests queue, then time out as 503.

Evidence chain — the config log and deploy record agree:

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 02:12:00 | `dep-4471` starts |
| 02:12:12 | `reload requested by deploy pipeline, generation 118 -> 119` |
| 02:13:41 | `generation 119 applied: 3 keys changed` |
| 02:13:41 | `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true` |
| 02:14:00 | `dep-4471` finishes |
| 02:14:14 | first slow-acquire warning |
| **02:14:18** | **first 503** |

19 seconds from deploy finish to first error.

## Impact window

**Start:** 2026-03-14 **02:14:18 UTC** (first 503, `req-07401`)
**End:** not yet — still erroring at 03:59:27, where the log ends
**Duration:** at least **1h 45m**

Error rate:

| Window | 503 rate |
|---|---|
| 01:00 – 02:14 | 0% |
| 02:14 – 02:20 | 44% (ramping) |
| 02:20 – 03:59 | **83%, flat** |

**530 total 503s.** Every one paired 1:1 with `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED`. The pool reads `in_use 20` of `size 20` on every single occurrence. Queue depth peaked at 271 waiting.

Wait times degraded steadily: 100ms at onset → 890ms by 03:59.

**Blast radius:** all five product routes, hit equally — `/v1/cart`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/session` (106 failures each). All four upstreams affected. This is not one bad service.

**`/health` returned 200 throughout.** It doesn't touch the pool. Health checks stayed green while 83% of real traffic failed — that's why nobody was paged for **67 minutes**:

```
03:21:05.282Z WARN ops paged on-call: error_rate 5m avg is 71%
```

## Roll back

### `dep-4471`

```
dep-4471,gateway,2026-03-14T02:12:00Z,2026-03-14T02:14:00Z,a.novak,
config: connection-per-request for pool isolation
```

Revert gateway config to **generation 118**. Or set `gateway.pool.perRequest` back to `false` directly — that one key is the cause.

If the pool isolation this deploy was going for is still wanted, it needs a much larger pool first. 20 is nowhere near enough for connection-per-request at this traffic level.

Note the deploy also raised `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs` 2000 → 2500. Not a cause, but it goes back with the rollback.

### Don't roll back these

`dep-4472` (billing-svc, 02:41) and `dep-4473` (catalog-svc, 03:20) both shipped **during** the incident. Neither caused anything — the 503 rate was already flat at 83% before both and didn't move after either.

Worth flagging separately: two teams kept deploying while the gateway was failing 8 in 10 requests. Nobody halted the pipeline.

## Open items for the next shift

**1. Verify the other nodes.** The log header says **node-3 of 3**. I only have one node's log. Assume all three are affected — the config reload was fleet-wide — but confirm it.

**2. Fix the health check.** `/health` doesn't exercise the connection pool, so it stayed green through a near-total outage. This is the detection gap that cost an hour. It should acquire a pooled connection.

**3. Separate issue — worker slowdown.** Not related to this incident, not paged, but real:

Worker job times climb linearly all night. 200ms → 2200ms, about **+11ms per minute**, dead steady. All six job types at the same rate. `db_wait` stays flat, so it isn't the database.

It does **not** start or bend at 02:14 — it's already climbing at 01:00, the first line of the log. Independent of the gateway.

Suspect `dep-4470` (worker, j.tanaka, "retry backoff for webhook jobs"), finished 00:55 — five minutes before the log starts. Unproven; the log doesn't reach back far enough to show a healthy baseline.

Jobs still succeed, so it's quiet. At this slope it won't stay quiet. Worth its own ticket.

**4. Known, unrelated.** One worker WARN at 02:36 — slow `SELECT * FROM orders` unindexed scan, already tracked as OPS-2210.
